normalized_selections.hypothesis: For oxidative addition into a deactivated heteroaryl chloride, a bulky electron-rich biarylphosphine (XPhos) precatalyst at high temperature (~104 C), high Pd loading (2.5%), and a few minutes residence time should give the highest conversion in this menu.
normalized_selections.reason: 3-Chloropyridine is a difficult C-Cl electrophile; XPhos-type Pd precatalysts are the canonical high-activity choice, and the combination of near-maximal temperature, maximal catalyst fraction, and intermediate (~4 min) residence time balances fast oxidative addition with limited protodehalogenation/catalyst decay. Alternatives here are either low temperature (30 C, kinetically dead), poor ligands for aryl chlorides (PPh3, XantPhos), or high temperature with very short time and lower loading.
